chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Back in New York with Slam Stewart at the Three Deuces
summary: After discharge he rejoined Slam Stewart with Billy Taylor and Harold West; the owner Sammy Kaye managed Slam, so they stayed at the club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I stayed in the army for quite awhile, and I started to -- Vernon tried to get me to stay in San Francisco but I didn't see any musical future there, you know, and so I had to get back to New York. So I went back to New York and I started -- I went to work with Slam Stewart, and Errol Gardner had just left Slam and Billy Taylor was the pianist. And it was Harold West, Slam Stewart, Billy Taylor and myself. We worked for quite a while, we did quite a bit of work, you know. And we lived on the street because Sammy Kaye, the owner of
Three Deuces, was Slam's manager, so that meant that we stayed there, most of the time, you know.
